title: One answer to what an attempt changed that no task declares, and a committed task always closes
description: In stage 1's a1c the restore point the base's suite parked under .claude/audit-backups/ was left out of the task commit by commit-task-work (it reads _manifest_io.PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE) and then refused by audit-task done's _uncommitted_leftovers, which skips only bookkeeping and run-state paths. Three readers compute the same question with their own skip lists (commit-task-work attempt_refusal, audit-task _uncommitted_leftovers, drive-phase's set-aside split), and a fix to one has twice missed another.
desiredOutcome: The commit step, the close and the writer's set-aside ask one shared function what an attempt changed that no in_progress task declares, so a path the plugin owns is never refused by one of them after another left it out; and a task whose work the drive committed closes on that commit instead of being offered no-change or retry

findings.issue: The close now leaves out every PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE row, including the plugin's own `.claude/audit.config.json` and `.claude/.gitignore`, whether git tracks them or not. A task that edits a TRACKED config without declaring it used to be refused by the close as an undeclared change made during the attempt. It is now named in an informational line and the close goes ahead with that edit left uncommitted. The commit step already did the same (ctw-at7 pins the config as left out), so the two readers agree, which is the point of the task. But the new lo-po cases pin only the restore point; none pins a tracked config edit, so the widening is unexamined.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.7-3y3 (794aa0d817c8): Keep the commit and the close in agreement, since exempting only untracked config in the close alone would bring back the divergence this task removes. Add a case in test_audit_task for a tracked `.claude/audit.config.json` edited during the attempt, so the behaviour is pinned either way. If the owner wants a tracked config edit refused, change the table row or the shared function once so both readers follow.

findings.issue: The comment says the scan is 'on what the readers MAY NOT NAME rather than on the instance that was found', and the task asked for the invariant, not the instance. What sc-ua5 does is a name blacklist: plugin_owned_under, PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE, attempt_strays and logs_dir. A reader that hardcodes `.claude/audit-backups`, keeps its own `under_any` list, or imports the table under another alias passes it (an `ImportFrom` alias is not a Name node). sc-ua6 only counts calls to `undeclared_changes`. It does not stop a reader from filtering the result again with a skip list of its own. The comment and docstring promise more than the check delivers.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.7-3y3 (794aa0d817c8): Either state the limit in the comment ('names the three primitives that were found; a differently spelled skip list is not seen') or widen the check to something the readers share. For example, assert that each reader has no local `skip`/`bookkeeping` list beyond its documented bookkeeping argument, and that it does not call `status_paths` or `under_any` itself.

findings.issue: The tree-wide scan passes on `outside == []` without counting the files it read. If the `os.walk(_output.SCRIPTS_DIR)` found no `.py` (a wrong anchor, or a skipped directory), the check would read as 'nobody else reads plugin_owned_under' and stay green. That is a filter narrowing to nothing, the shape the repo's no-silent-pass rule names. sc-ua7 shows the per-source scan can fail, but not that this walk reaches files.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.7-3y3 (794aa0d817c8): Collect the scanned names and assert the walk reached the home modules (`_manifest_io.py` and `_scoped_commit.py` among the files read) and more than a handful of files. Put the count in the check text so a narrowed walk goes red.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a commit after the attempt's start head carrying the task's Audit-Row": own_commit takes nonces from every journal row naming the task in ANY attempt (the loop at ~3795 filters on taskId only, not on rows after the current attempt's task.start row), and runs `git rev-list <start>..HEAD` without checking that `start` is an ancestor of HEAD. After a rebase or reset the recorded start head can survive off HEAD's history, `start..HEAD` then lists every commit since the merge base, and a previous attempt's still-reachable carrier is taken as this attempt's commit and closed on. _scoped_commit.attempt_span (_scoped_commit.py ~1234-1262) states it is the ONLY reader of the attempt's span and answers (None, why) for exactly this case; own_commit is a second reader with a different rule, the shape that docstring warns about. Read from the code; not run.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Do not run rev-list directly: check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <start> HEAD` (non-zero or error returns None, so the caller keeps the no-change decision) or read the span through _scoped_commit.attempt_span, and limit nonces to journal rows after the current attempt's task.start row.

findings.issue: A commit that was later reverted still closes the task. own_commit returns the Audit-Row carrier C without asking whether C's work is still in HEAD; after `git revert C` the carrier is still in start..HEAD, and the done --commit path (which asks whether the attempt changed a declared file in the span) also still sees C change it, so the task is recorded done on a commit whose effect is undone.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Require that the declared files still differ between C^ and HEAD in C's direction, e.g. no commit in C..HEAD touches the declared files, or `git diff --quiet C HEAD -- <declared>` is false-then-equal to C's own change; otherwise return None so the old decision stands.

findings.issue: The carrier's subject header is not checked. _invariants.recorded_commits (_invariants.py ~784-790) counts a carrier as the scoped commit only when its subject opens with the class header AND the trailer is in the last paragraph, because a squash or any commit that absorbs the message keeps the trailer. own_commit checks only inLast, so a squash-absorbing commit in the range whose last paragraph ends with the trailer is accepted as the task's commit. The task commit's header is commit-task-work.message_parts' `<type>(<taskId>): audit - ...`.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Also require carrier subject to match the task commit's header shape for this task id (`(<taskId>): ` after the type), treating a non-matching carrier as not found, as recorded_commits does with `absorbed`.

findings.issue: No case pins the range. Mutation: replace `rev-list start..HEAD` with `rev-list HEAD` (drop the range). tcc3's carrier sits after the start head, so it is found either way; no case has a carrier at or before the start head that must be ignored. The task clause is literally 'a commit after the attempt's start head'.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Add a case where a carrier exists before the attempt's start (a previous attempt's commit, or a start recorded after the commit) and own_commit/next must still answer no-change.

findings.issue: No case pins the `inLast` filter. Mutation: delete `if c["inLast"]` from the `held` set. Every carrier the fixture produces has its trailer in the last paragraph, so the filter never rejects anything.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Add a case whose range holds a commit with the Audit-Row line in a non-last paragraph and assert it is not closed on.

findings.issue: No case pins the withdrawn-nonce filter. Mutation: delete `nonce not in withdrawn`. The fixture journal has no audit.commit.withdrawn row, so the filter never fires and a withdrawn row's nonce would be accepted with no case red.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Add a case with a withdrawal row for the task's nonce plus a commit still carrying that trailer, and assert no-change is still offered.

findings.issue: No case pins the `task.get("commit")` guard (and none the status guard). Mutation: drop `or task.get("commit")` from the first line of own_commit. Every close_task call in tcc1-4 has an in_progress task with commit null, so the dropped guard changes no outcome.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Unit-call own_commit with a task that has a recorded commit and a carrier in range, and assert None.

findings.issue: tcc4 never produces a carrier: the stub returns 'nothing to commit' and no commit-task-work run happens, so there is no Audit-Row row and no carrier commit anywhere, and own_commit returns None at the first 'not carried' exit. It would stay green for the four mutations above together (drop the range, the inLast filter, the withdrawn filter and the commit guard), so it is not the twin that keeps the fix from firing on everything. It also leaves unpinned the unreadable-start-head and unreadable-journal exits, which the docstring promises return None.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.5-3y3 (5101bd4d4980): Make the twin a case with a real carrier that must be ignored (before start, withdrawn, or not in the last paragraph) and add the start-head-missing / journal-unreadable cases.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'extend tools/sweep-selftests.py's watched set to the checkout's own .claude/ so a write there is a finding naming the suite': CLAUDE_UNWATCHED removes state, logs, usage, worktrees, settings.local.json and audit-panel.json from the watched set, and those are most of the places the plugin writes under .claude/ (the checkout's .gitignore already lists state/, usage/ and logs/). The executor's own known offender, tests/test_audit_task.py writing .claude/state/{.gitignore,bash-writes-plugin-cli.json,writer-token.json} when TMPDIR sits in a clone, passes this guard unseen. A suite that exercises the usage ledger, a hook log or worktree creation against its own location would be invisible the same way. The exemption is by subtree name, so it hides every suite write there along with the live session's.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.6-3y3 (990bfa8c43d0): Narrow the exemption from a subtree to what the live session really writes. Options: (a) for state/logs/usage, watch the NAMES a suite is known to leak (writer-token.json, bash-writes-plugin-cli.json, state/.gitignore) with a case per name; (b) have sweep() refuse or loudly report when the scratch root (TMPDIR) is under the watched checkout, since that is the precondition for the unwatched leak (this overlaps P137.4, so the task may only file the cheap loud line); (c) at least add a case pinning which known suite-writes are NOT caught, so the blind spot is a recorded fact and not only a comment.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'a write there is a finding naming the suite': a write attributed to a suite is passed to grade() as debris, but grade() returns 'exited N' (or the raw timeout text) before it reads debris. A suite that writes into .claude/ and also exits non-zero or times out therefore gets no finding, and the write is not put in the loose row either, so it is lost. This is the very case the task reproduces: with TMPDIR in a clone, test_migrate_manifest.py writes audit-backups/ and then dies with FileNotFoundError, so the sweep shows only 'exited 1' and never names the write. The executor notes this as a limit, but the diff leaves it in place.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.6-3y3 (990bfa8c43d0): In sweep(), when the graded row is not ok and by_suite holds lines for it, append claude_debris(...) to the row's why. Or move those lines into `loose` so claude_row reports them. Add a case with a suite that writes into .claude/ and then exits 1.

findings.issue: The 'never blame a clean suite' rule (comment at 144-153) does not hold for deletions and for added directories. A DELETED entry is timed by the nearest surviving ancestor's mtime in the AFTER snapshot, and an ADDED directory by its own mtime. A directory's mtime moves with any later entry change directly under it, including entries the guard does not watch (state/ appearing, settings.local.json rewritten by rename, __pycache__). Example: suite A deletes .claude/keep at t1, and the live session or suite B then touches a direct child of .claude/ at t2. The deletion is stamped t2 and pinned on whichever single suite holds t2, which may be a clean one. cw6 asserts the stamps against fixed numbers (99, 66) and cannot see this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.6-3y3 (990bfa8c43d0): Do not time a deletion (or an added directory) from a directory stamp that other changes can move. Give it at=None and report it in the loose row naming every suite whose window overlaps the whole sweep, with its own wording. The current loose text for at=None says 'no suite's run holds the moment', which is untrue of a deletion that has no moment.

findings.issue: The 20 ms start slack is applied to every window, so at --jobs 1 two adjacent suites' windows overlap by up to the slack whenever the gap between one ended_ns and the next began_ns is shorter than it. A write in the last milliseconds of a suite then has two candidates, and the printed advice ('Re-run ... with --jobs 1 to name the one that wrote') can loop back to 'unattributed'. cw0 passes only because the writer sleeps 0.4 s after writing. The comment says windows 'cannot overlap' at --jobs 1.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.6-3y3 (990bfa8c43d0): Resolve ties on the raw windows first: if exactly one raw (unslacked) window holds the moment, name it; use the slack only when no raw window does. Add a case with a write at ended_ns - 1 ms and a neighbour starting 5 ms later.

findings.file: CLAUDE.md (tests section), CONTRIBUTING.md, tests/_harness.py fixture_root docstring
findings.issue: These documents say the watched pair is the working directory and the home directory. This diff adds a third watched directory, so those sentences are now false. The executor deferred them, and CLAUDE.md says that paragraph is not checked against the runner, so nothing will catch the drift.
findings.resolution: fixed in P137.6-3y3 (990bfa8c43d0): Update the three sentences in this task or file a follow-up task for them. Do not leave 'the watched pair' standing.

findings.issue: The docstring and the guide say the TMPDIR 'is left in place afterwards, and removing it is the task's teardown, which finds it through that record'. No teardown exists: nothing under plugins/audit/scripts removes the scratch or reads a *.tmpdir file (the same paragraph admits 'nothing in the drive reads the path back today'). The TMPDIRs, which hold whatever fixtures a writer's suites built, previously sat in the project's gitignored state dir and now accumulate in the machine's system temp, once per session (writer and reviewer, every round), with a record file nobody consumes. The sentence names a mechanism that is not there.
findings.resolution: Reword to say no teardown reads the record yet, and file a follow-up task for the drive to remove the TMPDIRs the scratch records name when it closes the task (or have the runner remove its own TMPDIR after the child exits, since the stream already carries the evidence).

findings.issue: A parent temp directory with a .git above it is refused with exit 5 and no other root is tried. That blocks a user who worked before this change: TMPDIR set inside the project, or a Windows user whose TEMP (under the profile) has a dotfiles repo at the profile root. The task says to 'refuse to start when no temp root outside a checkout exists'; the diff refuses when the one gettempdir() returned is inside a checkout, even though /tmp or /var/tmp may exist outside one. The refusal does name the directory and the remedy, and ras34 pins that it makes nothing, so this is a deliberate narrowing, not a silent one.
findings.resolution: Either keep the strict reading and say in the guide that a caller whose temp is inside a checkout must repoint TMPDIR, or try the remaining tempfile candidates (/tmp, /var/tmp) and refuse only when none is outside a checkout.

findings.issue: The suite's root comes from tempfile.mkdtemp under the ambient TMPDIR, and every _run now makes its parent temp under that root. If the suite is run with TMPDIR inside a checkout (the P137.3 scenario) the new refusal fires in every case, so the whole file goes red with exit 5 instead of naming the cause, and ras32's '_git_above(seen_tmp) is None' premise is no longer independent of the environment.
findings.resolution: Assert up front that root has no .git ancestor (one case naming the ambient TMPDIR), so a bad environment reads as that and not as 40 unrelated failures.

findings.issue: own_commit now reads the attempt's start through a local copy of start_head_of's row predicate (action task.start, details.taskId, details.attempt == task attempts). The docstring says it is found by the same three fields, so two readers of one row exist and agree only while nobody edits one. The executor disclosed this (the file is outside the task's files); R4 itself is about own_commit being a second reader beside attempt_span, and this reintroduces the same shape one level down.
findings.resolution: File a follow-up that adds a start_row_of(rows, task) to _scoped_commit.py, has start_head_of read its head from it and has own_commit read the moment from it; drop _attempt_start_moment.

findings.issue: The task-commit header is respelled as the regex ^[^\s()]+\(<taskId>\): . commit-task-work.message_parts builds the header as `<type>(<taskId>): audit - <subject>` where type is the manifest's meta.commit.type, any non-empty string after strip(); a type containing whitespace or parentheses (for example `feat(audit)`) gives a header this regex does not match. own_commit then returns None for the task's real commit and the caller offers no-change, which is the fault P137.2 fixed, reintroduced for that configuration. R6 asked for the header shape recorded_commits uses (a caller-supplied header prefix), not a new pattern. No case pins a non-default type.
findings.resolution: Match on what the task id pins rather than on the type: accept a subject containing `(<taskId>): ` after a non-empty prefix (str.find, no character class), or build the expected header from commit-task-work.message_parts with the manifest, as recorded_commits' header argument does. Add one oc case with meta.commit.type holding a space or parenthesis.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause (P137-R13, 'a write there is a finding naming the suite' even when the suite failed; task title 'names it even when the suite also failed'): grade() now reports the finding beside a non-zero exit, but `if code is None: return row(False, output)` still runs first, so a suite that wrote into the checkout's .claude/ and then TIMED OUT keeps its attributed lines in by_suite and they are dropped: not in the suite's row, not in the loose row. R13 named 'or the raw timeout text' explicitly. The docstring reasons 'the fixtures its kill left are the kill's, not the suite's', which is true of the cwd and home channels and false of a write into the checkout's .claude/, which no kill makes. cw14's g_late only drives a working-directory finding, so the checkout channel on a timeout is unpinned. The executor's descriptive claim ('names it even when the suite also failed') overstates the diff for this case.
findings.resolution: In grade() let the kill exemption apply only to the cwd/home findings: for code None, still append findings whose channel is CLAUDE_CHANNEL ('timed out; and wrote into the checkout .claude: ...'). Add a cw14 case: code None with debris=['checkout .claude: ADDED stray.txt'] must name stray.txt.

findings.issue: The refusal-to-start behaviour that tests.add names ('a temp dir inside a checkout is refused') is pinned only on the helper. cw15 calls scratch_refusal() directly; nothing runs main() or reads its exit code, so deleting the four lines in main() that call it leaves every case, and the gate, green. The documents (CONTRIBUTING.md paragraph, _harness.py docstring, cw16) all say the sweep 'refuses to start'. Shape: an assertion the behaviour (the call and `return 2`) never reaches.
findings.resolution: Add a case that drives main() (or a thin wrapper taking tmp) with a temp dir containing a .git above it and asserts exit 2 plus the 'refusing to start' text on stderr, and a clean temp dir that does not take that exit.

findings.issue: The exemptions are largely evidence-backed: each pattern matches names present in .claude/state of the live checkout with mtimes from the current session (call-start, journal-preimage, plan-gate, bash-writes, tdd-reminder, running-plugin, attempts, briefs, drive), and every writer cited resolves to a constant. But the table's rule 'a name that command did not list is not in this table' turns absence from a 240-minute sample into 'not written by the session'. `bash-writes-plugin-<sid>.json` is written by the live PostToolUse hook (plugins/audit/hooks/journal-writes.py:1225-1260, record_plugin_write) the first time a plugin script journals a new rel in a session; the row's own sentence admits it is 'not left out', and cw5 pins `state/bash-writes-plugin-<sid>.json` as a SUITE's file. A sweep typed inside a session at that moment (the checkout holds bash-writes-plugin-cli.json and -panel.json from the same hook) goes red once on a session write; it clears on re-run, which is the 'guard gets routed around' shape the file's comments warn about.
findings.resolution: Add a row for `^state/bash-writes-plugin-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.json$` citing record_plugin_write, and move the plugin-sidecar example from cw5's `theirs` to `live`. Derive the writer list from the hooks' own filename constants rather than from a time-windowed ls.

findings.issue: cw10's 'a character wrong' variant is always `state/` -> `state/x`, a prefix change. A row loosened at its tail or anchor (e.g. `\.json$` becoming `\.json`, or `(?:-[0-9a-f]+)?` becoming `.*`) still skips its example and still fails to match the prefix-mutated one, so cw10 stays green. The new gate-parity comment and the case text claim a row 'grown loose enough to swallow a suite's file' is reported; the mutation only reaches prefix looseness.
findings.resolution: Also test a tail mutation per row (append 'x' to the example, and for the directory rows a sibling like 'state/briefs-extra/x'), and assert the sentence.

findings.issue: The structural scan (result_scan, sc-ua10/sc-ua11) can be fooled by a reader that hands the narrowed list to a helper, and the comment claims more than it delivers. Taint is only set by `x = R["during"]` (a direct Subscript, line 300-303); an assignment from a call (`during = _drop_config(strays["during"])`, or `during = _drop_config(during)` after the tainted assignment) taints nothing, and a Call argument is never examined, so nothing is flagged. The helper itself is not scanned either: only functions that call `undeclared_changes` are walked (line 268), so a comprehension over its parameter is invisible. Passing the WHOLE answer to a helper is caught (`used other than by key`), but passing a list read by key is not. Further holes in the same shape: a `for p in R["during"]` loop that appends in an else branch rather than using `continue` (325-329); `_only_membership` accepts any comparator that is not a literal and not an upper-case Name, so `p not in _skiplist()`, `p in _mio.SKIP` (Attribute) and a lower-case module list all count as 'computed' (251-253); a tuple-unpacked or `or`-wrapped read is not tainted. The comment at 207-217 says the lists may be narrowed 'by a membership test ... and by nothing else' and that a reader has 'no way to rebuild it ... handing it on' - false for the helper route. The docstring at _scoped_commit.py:~1160 does admit 'a reader that reaches a skip by a route neither describes is not caught', which satisfies the first alternative of P137-R2, but the helper hand-off is the most obvious such route and is cheap to close. Read from the code; not run.
findings.resolution: Make taint transitive: an Assign whose value contains any tainted name or a by-key read of an UNDECLARED_KEYS list taints its targets (any expression, including calls, BoolOps, tuples). Flag a tainted value passed as an argument to any call except a short allowlist of presentation builtins (len, sorted, set, list, tuple, str.join) and, for a same-file helper receiving it, scan that helper's body with its parameter as tainted. Narrow `_only_membership` to a comparator that is a bare lower-case Name bound in the function from something other than a literal, and flag loops that filter without `continue` (any `if` guarding an append of the loop variable). Add a sc-ua11 mutation per hole (call-wrapped, helper, Attribute comparator). Or reword the comment so it does not say 'nothing else'.

findings.issue: `_is_tracked` returns True when git cannot answer, which is the loud direction for the commit and the close (the config counts as an undeclared change and the verb refuses; nothing is written) but the unsafe one for the set-aside. There `plugin_owned_rels` is read as a PROTECTION list (`plugin_owned_paths` -> `settle_aside`: 'Nothing is reverted ... when one of paths is plugin-owned'). A config wrongly judged tracked is not in that list, so it is reverted by `git checkout HEAD` or, when HEAD does not hold it, deleted by `os.remove` (drive-phase.py:3685-3691). Reaching that needs `ls-files` to fail (or `plan_to_git` to return None) while `ls-tree` and `checkout` succeed, so it is narrow, and the patch keeps the bytes; but one function now serves three readers with opposite safe directions and the diff chose the direction by the two that refuse. `plan_to_git` None (outside the checkout) is also read as tracked, though nothing outside the checkout is listed by status in the first place. Judgement from reading; sc-ua9's `blind_rows` pins only the 'not exempted' side and no case pins the set-aside side of a failed answer.
findings.resolution: Return a tri-state from `_is_tracked` (tracked / untracked / unknown) and let `plugin_owned_rels` place the config for the refusing readers when unknown, while `plugin_owned_paths` treats unknown as owned (protected), or have set_aside refuse to revert a path whose tracked state is unknown. Add a case with git unavailable for the set-aside reader.

findings.issue: The change edits tests/test_drive_phase.py, which is in neither the task's `files` nor its `tests.gate` (the gate is the three suites test__scoped_commit, test_audit_task, test_commit_task_work). The behaviour change really does turn xs6 red (a tracked config is no longer plugin-owned for the set-aside), so the recorded gate run, which passed, would have passed over a stale xs6; only the executor's own wider gate command ran it. The brief's diff also omits the file, so a reader of the brief does not see the set-aside's new expectation. The outcome does describe the xs6 change, so the claim is honest; the scope declaration is not.
findings.resolution: Add tests/test_drive_phase.py to the task's files and to tests.gate (retarget --gate-set) so the dependant suite is part of the recorded gate, or record the widening as a scope note on the task.

review.outcome: [findings: 28 - 0 high, 6 med, 22 low; 16 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: One function answers which paths an attempt changed that no in_progress task declares, and every reader asks it
tasks.description: Move the question - paths changed during the attempt (by the start snapshot, else mtime against startedAt) that no in_progress task covers, with the plan's bookkeeping, the plugin's run state and every _manifest_io.PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE row taken out and returned separately as named plugin-owned state - into one function in _scoped_commit, and make commit-task-work.py's attempt refusal, audit-task.py's _uncommitted_leftovers (the close) and drive-phase.py's set-aside split call it, deleting their own skip lists. The close then never refuses a path the commit step left out as plugin-owned. Add a case per reader in which a restore point appears under .claude/audit-backups/ during the attempt: the commit leaves it out and names it, and the close on that commit is accepted; and a lint or case that fails when a reader computes the skip list itself (the invariant, not the instance).

add: tests/test_audit_task.py: a close on a task commit is accepted when a plugin-owned restore point under .claude/audit-backups/ appeared during the attempt, and the close names it
tests/test__scoped_commit.py: the shared function returns plugin-owned state apart from the undeclared changes, and every reader of the question calls it

outcome.technical: Added _scoped_commit.undeclared_changes(git_root, project, config, record, started_at, owned, bookkeeping) -> (changes, why): status_paths, drops the reader's bookkeeping and run_state_rels, splits covered-by-owned, splits every PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE row (plugin_owned_rels/split_plugin_owned, moved here from commit-task-work), then attribute(); returns attribute's dict plus covered, strays, pluginOwned.
